land.text: Khorasan, the governorate given to Tahir ibn Husayn in 821 as a reward for his support of al-Ma'mun in the Fourth Fitna

predecessors.note: Cliopatria has no Tahirid row; its Abbasid shape for 821 covers 2,104 of the 2,206 gazetteer cells of Khorasan (checked with tools/gazetteer.py), which the map should draw in the Tahirid colour as a governorate with wide autonomy.

land.text: Khorasan, annexed by Ya'qub ibn al-Layth in 873 (Herat already taken in 870)
Transoxiana, where Samanid governors had served under Tahirid overlordship; the pages opened give no year for the Samanids' independence

successors.note: Samanid page: Tahirid authority had weakened after defeats by Ya'qub al-Saffar, leaving the Samanids more or less independent.

capitals.name: Merv (Mary)
capitals.note: Infobox: "Merv, later Nishapur"; no page opened gives the year of the move, so the split at 830 (Abdallah "only arrived in Nishapur in 830") is bridging.

capitals.name: Nishapur (Neyshabur)
capitals.note: Abdallah ibn Tahir arrived at Nishapur in 830 and settled there; it fell to the Saffarids in 873.

rulers.name: Tahir ibn Husayn
rulers.note: Governor of Khorasan; died soon after taking office

rulers.name: Abdallah ibn Tahir
rulers.note: text of the page says he died in 844, infobox and table 845; Abdallah ibn Tahir page: "either at the end of 844 or in 845"

correction.text: Khorasan with the Transoxiana cities governed by the Samanid brothers: "In 821, Tahir was made governor of Khorasan"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Tahirid row). Infobox area 1,000,000 km2 (given for "800 est."); Khorasan plus Transoxiana in the gazetteer is about 1.02 M km2, so the ratio is about 1.0. Transoxiana was held through Samanid governors (vassal tint, see ledger).

correction.text: Khorasan, Transoxiana and Zarang in Sistan, occupied by the Tahirids in 828

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Zarang occupied after the Kharijite leader died in 828 ("never collected taxes in the surrounding countryside"), so only the city is added.

correction.text: Khorasan, Transoxiana, Zarang and Tabaristan after the fall of Mazyar in 839

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Mazyar's Tabaristan passes to the Tahirids in 839 ("This left the Tahirids as the rulers of Tabaristan, and Qarin I was restored as the ruler of the Bavand dynasty as a vassal").

correction.text: Khorasan, Transoxiana and Tabaristan; Zarang and Sistan lost to the Saffarid rebels

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Sistan's administrative dependency lost to rebels under Tahir II (845-862); the Saffarid page's infobox dates the Saffarid state to 861, the year used here (the Tahirid page gives no year).

correction.text: Khorasan and Transoxiana; Tabaristan lost to Hasan ibn Zayd

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Tabaristan declares for the Zaydi Hasan ibn Zayd in 864; Sulayman ibn Abdallah chased him out in 865 but he "returned that same year and recovered the province".

correction.text: Khorasan and Transoxiana without Herat, captured by the Saffarids in 870

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "The Tahirid city of Herat was captured in 870"; the rest of Khorasan falls in 873.

region.text: Khorasan: "In 821, Tahir was made governor of Khorasan"

ledger.note: 821: al-Ma'mun's general Tahir is made governor of Khorasan, the start of the Tahirid dynasty. "In 821, Tahir was made governor of Khorasan" (infobox: established 821); he had also been military governor of Baghdad since 820.

region.text: Samarkand, Farghana and Tashkent, held by the sons of Asad ibn Saman as governors under the governor of Greater Khorasan

ledger.note: 821: Transoxiana's governors answer to the governor of Khorasan. The Samanid page: Ghassan ibn Abbad, 'governor of Greater Khorasan', gave Samarkand, Farghana, Tashkent and Herat to the four sons of Asad in 819, and a Tahirid governor (Muhammad ibn Tahir) appointed Ibrahim ibn Ilyas in 856; the start year is bridging, taken from the Tahirid takeover of Khorasan.
828: Talha occupies Zarang, the city of Sistan. 'After their leader died in 828, the Tahirids occupied Zarang but never collected taxes in the surrounding countryside.'
830: Abdallah ibn Tahir settles at Nishapur. 'He only arrived in Nishapur in 830'; the Tahirid page names the capitals 'Merv, later Nishapur'.

region.text: Tabaristan: "the Tahirids as the rulers of Tabaristan"

ledger.note: 839: Mazyar is betrayed and handed over; Tabaristan passes to the Tahirids. 'This left the Tahirids as the rulers of Tabaristan, and Qarin I was restored as the ruler of the Bavand dynasty as a vassal.' The Abdallah ibn Tahir page adds that in 839 he got the caliph to act against Mazyar, who was executed.

region.text: Sistan: "Sistan's administrative dependency was lost to rebels"

ledger.note: 861: Sistan lost to the Saffarid rebels. The Tahirid page says only that 'Sistan's administrative dependency was lost to rebels' during Tahir II's rule (845-862); 861 is the Saffarid page's infobox date for the dynasty (Ya'qub 'seized control of the Sistan region', no year given).

region.text: Tabaristan: "declaring their allegiance to the independent Zaydi ruler Hasan ibn Zayd in 864"

ledger.note: 864: Tabaristan rebels and 'declaring their allegiance to the independent Zaydi ruler Hasan ibn Zayd in 864' (Tahirid page, same year). Hasan page: 'a rebellion broke out in Ruyan, Kalar, and Chalus, and the rebels called on Hasan to lead them.'

region.text: Tabaristan, where Sulayman ibn Abdallah ibn Tahir opposed Hasan

ledger.note: 864: the Tahirids fight for Tabaristan; the Tahirid viceroy Sulayman ibn Abdallah ibn Tahir was Hasan's main opponent.

region.text: Tabaristan: Hasan "returned that same year and recovered the province"

ledger.note: 865: Hasan holds Tabaristan. 'He was chased out of Tabaristan in 865 by Sulayman ibn Abdallah', but Hasan returned that same year and recovered the province (he held Gurgan from 867 and died at Amul in 884).
870: the Saffarids take Herat. 'The Tahirid city of Herat was captured in 870.'
870: Ya'qub's offensive against Khorasan begins with Herat (he 'began attacks on Khorasan, Khuzestan, Kerman and Fars'; the page dates only Herat, 870, and the annexation of Khorasan, 873).

region.text: Khorasan around Nishapur and Balkh: "annexing Khorasan in 873"

ledger.note: 873: the fighting ends with the Saffarid annexation of Khorasan.

region.text: Khorasan, annexed by the Saffarids in 873: "annexing Khorasan in 873"

ledger.note: 873: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth takes Khorasan and Nishapur. 'In 873 he was finally overthrown by the Saffarid dynasty' (Tahirid page); 'overthrew the Tahirid dynasty, annexing Khorasan in 873' (Saffarid page). Neither page gives a month.

region.text: Transoxiana, Samanid governors "more or less independent"

ledger.note: 873: Tahirid overlordship over Transoxiana ends with the dynasty. The Samanid page: Tahirid authority 'had significantly weakened after suffering several defeats to Saffarid ruler Ya'qub al-Saffar', leaving the Samanids more or less independent; no year is given for their independence.

region.text: Khorasan: "overthrown by the Saffarid dynasty" in 873

ledger.note: 873: the Tahirid dynasty ends. 'In 873 he was finally overthrown by the Saffarid dynasty'; the Saffarid Ya'qub ibn Layth captured Nishapur from Muhammad ibn Tahir.

wars.name: Tahirid campaigns against the Kharijites of Sistan
wars.outcome: Talha "failed to remove the Kharijites from Sistan"; after their leader died in 828 the Tahirids occupied Zarang but never collected taxes in the countryside.

wars.name: Revolt of Mazyar in Tabaristan
wars.outcome: Mazyar, who resisted Tahirid claims over his tribute, was captured and executed in 839; Tabaristan passed to the Tahirids with Qarin I restored as a Bavand vassal.
wars.note: The Mazyar page dates only his fall (839); the start of the revolt is not given.

wars.name: Hasan ibn Zayd's rebellion in Tabaristan
wars.outcome: The Zaydi Alid Hasan ibn Zayd was proclaimed emir in 864, chased out by Sulayman ibn Abdallah in 865 and returned the same year to recover the province.

wars.name: Saffarid conquest of Khorasan
wars.outcome: Ya'qub ibn al-Layth took Herat in 870 and annexed Khorasan in 873, ending the Tahirid dynasty.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines: the frontiers follow the governorate of Khorasan (Herat, Balkh, Merv, Nishapur) and the cities named; the Transoxiana and Zarang holdings are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria has no Tahirid row (the Abbasid shape includes Khorasan). Wikidata id not known (wikidata.org unreachable); left null. Not written as events: the Tahirid governorship of Baghdad (shurta from 820, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim for 25+ years, 865-866 interventions, replaced 891: a city governorship inside the Abbasid core, not territory); Abdallah's posting to Egypt (826-827, undated on the page); Tahirid suppression of movements in Transoxiana and campaigns against the Oghuz (no annexation, no years); Kerman, which no page ties to the Tahirids. Dates that differ: Abdallah's death 844/845; Muhammad's reign 862-872 (infobox) vs 873 (text). The 861 Sistan loss year is bridging. The Samanid brothers (Nuh, Ahmad, Yahya, Ilyas) are the vassal 'counterpart' of Transoxiana; the Samanid state proper is samanid-empire (me-08-b). Counterparts without dossiers: Mazyar of Tabaristan / Qarinvandids and the Bavandids (Tabaristan highlands, Qarin I as Tahirid vassal from 839); the Kharijites of Sistan. 'Sistan' and 'Zarang' resolve; no new gazetteer names.
